newsitem.title: USA: Labor agency issues complaint against Caterpillar.
newsitem.headline: Labor agency issues complaint against Caterpillar.

text.p: The National Labour Relations Board Wednesday brought new complaints against Caterpillar Inc., seeking back pay for workers who were allegedly mistreated after they offered to return to work after a strike ended in 1995.
The NLRB issued two complaints that charge Caterpillar did not promptly rehire striking workers as required by law and that it denied others jobs by keeping replacement workers on its payroll.
The complaints did not describe how much the company would owe the workers if an administrative law judge decides against Caterpillar.

But the United Auto Workers, which represented about 9,000 workers involved in the 17-month strike, said the two complaints and others lodged against the company create an estimated liability of $113 million for Caterpillar. The union said a hearing on the complaints has not been scheduled yet.
The heavy machinery maker had no immediate comment on the financial impact of the complaints, which were issued by NLRB Regional Director Glenn Zipp in Peoria.
In a statement, the company said the complaints ignore the efforts it made to bring striking employees back to work. It also said it will fight the charges.
"When UAW (union) leaders ended their lengthy strike, our goal was to ensure a smooth transition for everyone, while continuing to meet customer needs," Caterpillar said.
"We believe we acted properly and responsibly, accomplishing our goal in an amazingly short time, given the logistics involved." -- Reuter Chicago Newsdesk 312-408-8787
